starting_spirits.description: A record harvest is being pursued through an extraordinary diversion of labour, transport and fuel. The campaign is still under way on 1 January 1970; its historical shortfall must not be treated as a completed event.
starting_spirits.resolution: Harvest choices set the course. On 26 July 1970 replace, never stack, the campaign with a smaller recovery burden; the rebalancing programme clears it sooner.

starting_spirits.title: The Revolutionary Offensive
starting_spirits.description: The 1968 nationalisations extended state control deep into small enterprise. Political control is strong, but administrative overload and the disappearance of local initiative weigh on civilian production.
starting_spirits.resolution: Protected Enterprises or Joint Ventures replaces this with a defined reformed institution; no duplicate command-economy penalty.

starting_spirits.title: Sugar and Soviet Oil
starting_spirits.description: Sugar provides an export livelihood, while machinery and oil depend heavily on foreign partners. This is a structural exposure, not a guarantee of outside support.
starting_spirits.resolution: Food before Sugar and diversified industry reduce this exposure. A Soviet support withdrawal worsens the remaining dependency instead of imposing a scripted collapse regardless of prior policy.

starting_spirits.title: The American Embargo
starting_spirits.description: Restricted access to the American market and trade finance narrows Cuba's commercial options. The economic burden belongs to the continuing dispute and ends only through a real settlement or a change in the legal sanctions regime.
starting_spirits.resolution: An accepted US executive settlement may ease or end the 1970â€“90 trade embargo. Separate tariff, official credit and territorial issues remain subject to their own terms; do not apply later 1996 restrictions retroactively or duplicate a native/Imperia sanction.

starting_spirits.title: Committees of Defence
starting_spirits.description: The CDRs and security apparatus reach into daily life. Their defensive intelligence advantage is accompanied by political conformity and a narrower space for independent technical discussion.
starting_spirits.resolution: A constitutional/civic security settlement replaces, rather than silently retains, this institution. Historical PCC/FAR reform may professionalise it without claiming instant pluralism.

starting_spirits.title: Literacy and Public Medicine
starting_spirits.description: Literacy and public medicine have widened access to essential services. Maintaining that provision requires a lasting commitment of teachers, medical staff and public income.
starting_spirits.resolution: Shared social programmes improve provision through actual native budget tiers. Protect these accumulated services across government changes.

starting_spirits.title: A Revolution in Exile
starting_spirits.description: Exile has fractured families and removed professional networks. The continuing disruption of skills and confidence weighs on an already demanding economic transformation.
starting_spirits.resolution: Negotiated dialogue and registered voluntary return agreements through the existing diaspora system reduce the burden. No focus invents a mass return or coerced migration count.

CUB receives one 25% industry research bonus and an active assistance programme: sanction resistance +15%, foreign influence defence -15%.
SOV receives +15 bilateral opinion; no subject status, forced faction membership or automatic funding stream.
soviet_assistance.guard: Both exist and are at peace with each other; pending offer expires after 90 days; repeat acceptance cannot repeat payment or research.
soviet_assistance.custom: New bilateral event/receipt glue using native money, opinion and research APIs.

cmea_admission.title: CMEA Admission
terms: Acceptance grants the actual COLDWAR_CUB_cmea_member idea; no automatic money or factories.
Application costs CUB 0.10 Treasury only on accepted admission; member content requires this spirit in availability and reward guards.
cmea_admission.guard: Admission is before the member-only focus. Exit removes membership and suspends its active programme without replaying grants on readmission.
cmea_admission.custom: Cuba-specific admission contract. Main MD 2000 has no reusable general CMEA membership provider; integrate with Cold War Soviet commonwealth content rather than inventing a parallel economic simulator.

air_defence.title: Air Defence Training
terms: CUB pays 0.45 Treasury; SOV pays 0.15 Treasury on acceptance.
CUB receives one radar level in a legal Cuban state and one 25% radar research use; no aircraft or missiles are spawned.
air_defence.guard: Both governments consent; verify owned/controlled target and radar level cap before either charge.
air_defence.custom: New agreement glue; native building/research providers.

medical_mission.title: Requested Medical Mission
terms: CUB pays 0.15 Treasury; recipient pays 0.10 Treasury on acceptance.
Recipient receives healthcare expenditure -5% for 365 days; Cuba receives +15 bilateral opinion.
Cuba's Medical Brigades programme raises weekly healthcare expenditure by 10%; no workforce reduction or second flat upkeep debit.
medical_mission.guard: Recipient requests or accepts the mission, is not at war with Cuba, and has a working health budget. Refusal/expiry charges nobody.
medical_mission.custom: New Cuba diplomatic offer; does not treat a generic health-cost reduction as literal donated hospital equipment.

overseas_mission.title: Requested Overseas Assistance
overseas_mission.recipient: Independent eligible country at war, or agreed liberation partner
terms: An accepted request opens ordinary native military/volunteer diplomacy and a scoped advisory decision.
CUB pays 0.20 Treasury and recipient receives 15 army experience once; troop/equipment transfers use actual native stocks and consent.
No annexation, invented divisions, automatic war or generic occupation-state support shortcut.
overseas_mission.guard: Recipient controls its response. Angola/Ethiopia/Grenada are historical contexts, not 1970 pre-annexation targets. Recheck independence, war and available troops at use.
overseas_mission.custom: New recipient-owned request/receipt; no general Cuban Colonial Affairs provider currently exists.

us_normalisation.guard: Explicit US acceptance; check actual native US embargo/Imperia sanction state and remove only agreed restrictions. Exactly-once commission receipt prevents repeat payment. Neither talks nor Interests Sections alone remove the embargo.

chronology.title: The Ten Million Ton Harvest
chronology.trigger: The harvest campaign is unresolved; final national results are recorded at the July 26 review.

choices.title: Return Labour to the Wider Economy

chronology.history: On 19 May 1970 Fidel Castro publicly acknowledged that the ten-million-ton target would not be met. The 1970 harvest reached about 8.54 million metric tons, a record but short of the goal; final results were announced at the 26 July celebration. The campaign's labour and transport diversion left broader economic costs. Sources: https://cubanstudies.history.ufl.edu/gems-of-the-archive/the-ten-million-ton-harvest-of-1970/ ; https://ascecubadatabase.org/asce_proceedings/cubas-sugar-industry-in-the-1990s-potential-exports-to-the-u-s-and-world-markets/
chronology.duration: July 26 settlement: economic adjustments last 180 days; stability changes once. Remove the original campaign first; the separate recovery burden lasts 90/180 days by the completed harvest course.

chronology.title: Cuban Forces in Angola
chronology.trigger: Angola approaches independence amid civil war; the MPLA requests Cuban assistance and a lawful recipient relationship is available. The historical conflict and an independent consenting recipient must actually exist; the calendar alone cannot create either.

choices.title: Limit the Commitment to Advisers and Medical Teams

chronology.history: Cuba began a large military intervention in Angola in November 1975 after the MPLA sought its assistance; Cuban troops helped defend Luanda before independence on 11 November. This was an expeditionary commitment with substantial military and economic costs, not simply a volunteer programme. The scale and continuation remain contingent on Cuban decisions in alternate history. Source: https://history.state.gov/milestones/1969-1976/angola ; https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76v28/d132
chronology.duration: Active only while the accepted mission is operating. Withdraw or terminate the recipient agreement to remove both its benefits and recurring burdens; no free troops are created.

chronology.title: Interests Sections in Havana and Washington
chronology.trigger: Both governments consent to a limited diplomatic arrangement while the broader dispute remains unsettled.

choices.title: Open Reciprocal Interests Sections
effects: CUB and USA each pay 0.05 Treasury on mutual acceptance

choices.title: Defer the Arrangement
effects: No change to the embargo or diplomatic status

chronology.history: On 1 July 1977, both governments announced reciprocal Interests Sections, which opened on 1 September in the Swiss and Czechoslovak embassies respectively. This restored limited official contact; it did not normalize relations or end the statutory embargo. Source: https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v23/d18
chronology.duration: 365 days for the influence adjustment; offices and agreement receipt persist until mutually closed.

chronology.title: The Ogaden War
chronology.trigger: The Somali invasion of Ethiopia intensifies; Ethiopia requests Cuban assistance and the government must choose its level of commitment. The historical conflict and an independent consenting recipient must actually exist; the calendar alone cannot create either.
chronology.history: Cuban forces were deployed to Ethiopia during the 1977â€“78 Ogaden War, alongside Soviet support for Mengistu's government. The deployment followed earlier Cuban activity in Africa and carried real personnel and logistical costs. Source: https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v17/d103
chronology.duration: Active only while the accepted mission is operating. Withdraw or terminate the recipient agreement to remove both its benefits and recurring burdens; no free troops are created.

chronology.title: Dialogue with the Cuban Community Abroad
chronology.trigger: Representatives of the government and Cuban communities abroad agree to meet and define a limited humanitarian and family agenda.

choices.title: Implement the December Agreement
effects: Pardon 3,000 prisoners convicted of state-security offences and 600 convicted of emigration-law violations, as stated in the agreement
Register actual family migration through the existing migration ledger

chronology.history: On 8 December 1978, the Committee of 75 and Cuban government representatives signed an agreement on prisoners, family reunification and visits. The government announced pardon of 3,000 prisoners convicted of offences against state security or national integrity and 600 convicted under emigration provisions. It did not create a multiparty system or end political restrictions. Migration counts must use the existing ledger and must not subtract the same people twice. Source: https://cidh.oas.org/countryrep/Cuba79eng/chap.4.htm
chronology.duration: One-time humanitarian/legitimacy settlement. Programme effects do not repeat on reopening talks; any physical return requires a registered voluntary migration transaction.

chronology.title: The Havana Non-Aligned Summit
chronology.trigger: Cuba has accepted the 1979 summit hosting role through diplomacy. Cuba is already a NAM founding participant; no accession or guaranteed Soviet allegiance is implied.

choices.title: Press the Anti-Imperialist Platform
effects: Bilateral opinion with the Soviet Union +5

chronology.history: Cuba was a founding participant in the Non-Aligned Movement in 1961; the Havana summit of 3â€“9 September 1979 was a major expression of its chairmanship, not accession. Source: https://www.nam.go.ug/history ; https://www.nam.go.ug/previous-chairmanship-documents
chronology.duration: 365 days for programme modifiers; opinion/stability are one-time effects.

chronology.title: The Mariel Exodus
chronology.trigger: Only if a comparable asylum crisis and pent-up departure pressure actually arise under the revolutionary government. USA must consent to the reception/transport arrangement; no fixed historical total is removed automatically.

choices.title: Open Mariel for an Organised Departure
effects: Record actual emigrants once through the existing migration ledger

choices.title: Restrict Departures to Negotiated Cases
effects: Record only departures that actually occur

chronology.history: Cuban guards were withdrawn from the Peruvian embassy on 4 April 1980; the asylum crowd then grew rapidly. On 20 April Fidel Castro announced that the port of Mariel would be opened for departures, and the exodus continued until 26 September. About 125,000 people left; political coercion accompanied some departures. Historical totals belong in the existing migration ledger and should not also be removed by this event. Sources: https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v23/d89 ; https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1980/04/06/cuba-to-allow-exodus-of-1500-in-asylum-at-peruvian-embassy/b7b27181-ebfd-4dd8-960b-a4981c6497dd
chronology.duration: Stability is a one-time political effect; influence-defence adjustments last 180 days. Actual migration occurs only once through the population ledger.

chronology.title: Rectification of Errors and Negative Tendencies
chronology.trigger: Only under a PCC government. An earlier completed SDPE/Rectification verdict is respected; the congress cannot grant its economic programme again or bypass a mutually exclusive focus.

choices.title: Reaffirm the Mobilisation Programme
effects: Requires the Rectification verdict; Stability +2 percentage points once
No additional economic modifiers: the focus programme already supplies workforce +4%, construction +8%, civilian productivity -6%, research -3%

choices.title: Defend Enterprise Accounting
effects: Requires the Continue the SDPE verdict; Stability -1 percentage point and Political power +35 once
No additional economic modifiers: the focus programme already supplies civilian productivity +10%, agricultural productivity +10%, tax revenue -5%

choices.title: Refer the Question to the Economic Commission
effects: If no verdict is completed: Political power +15 once; the normal focus choice remains available
No automatic focus completion, duplicate programme or change of ruling party

chronology.history: At the Third PCC Congress in February 1986, the leadership began rectification, criticizing material incentives and aspects of the Soviet-inspired economic management system. It was a policy shift within one-party rule, not a return to Che Guevara or an automatic economic collapse. Source: https://www.jstor.org/stable/10.2307/45194255
chronology.duration: One-time congress settlement; focus programmes are never granted twice.

chronology.title: A Contraction in Soviet Trade and Supply
chronology.trigger: Only fire if actual Soviet deliveries, oil supply, or trade support to Cuba have materially fallen below the agreed scenario baseline; otherwise this contingency remains dormant.

choices.title: Protect Food, Health and Essential Transport
Seek Emergency Trade and Reschedule Imports

chronology.history: Soviet supply cuts intensified in August 1990; Fidel Castro formally declared the Special Period in September. Trade and credit disruption had begun earlier and deepened through the following years. This was not a complete Soviet cutoff on 1 January 1990 and should not impose inevitable collapse. Any resulting migration must pass through existing migration accounting. Dollar legalisation and major reforms associated with 1993 belong to later developments, not to this 1990 event. Sources: https://repositorio.cepal.org/bitstream/handle/11362/1030/4/ESLA1991v2_en.pdf ; https://ascecubadatabase.org/asce_proceedings/the-cuban-economic-crisis-of-the-1990s-and-the-external-sector/
chronology.duration: Emergency-choice modifiers last 365 days, with a separate exposure-scaled shortage spirit only for the verified duration of disrupted supply. Renewals require an explicit new policy decision and cannot stack.

setup.title: Proposed 1970 initialization
setup.text: The existing 1970 Cuba history has no education, health or corruption idea tiers. The edu_02/health_02 entries belong to 2000. This concept proposes edu_02, health_02 and corruption_level_04 when the corresponding category is genuinely uninitialized; preserve a valid existing tier. These are balance baselines for broad public provision and bureaucratic constraints, not historical statistical measurements. No 2000 Special Period or migration-crisis spirit is imported.
setup.guard: 1970 scenario, original CUB, one-time setup receipt; initialize only missing categories, recalculate native budget/law variables afterward.

lifecycles.title: The 1970 harvest
rules: The initial campaign is active on 1 January. Finish the Zafra programme modifiers expire at the 26 July review; Restore the Sectors is a lasting national reallocation.
The May announcement is informational. At the July review remove the original campaign and any temporary Finish the Zafra programme before applying the selected 180-day settlement.

Mobilisation or no completed harvest verdict: recovery burden = civilian industry productivity âˆ’6%, construction speed âˆ’4%, for 180 days. Rebalanced course: civilian industry productivity âˆ’3%, construction speed âˆ’2%, for 90 days. The timed July event choice is additional and explicitly listed.
A player starting late can resolve an overdue historical harvest once. There is no permanent +12% farm mobilisation from a finished 1970 campaign.

lifecycles.title: Ownership and the Revolutionary Offensive
rules: Protected Enterprises or Joint Ventures removes the original Revolutionary Offensive spirit. Its replacement is the chosen national economic programme with exactly the focus deltas; there is no second hidden reform bonus.

Shared ownership priorities survive a government change until formally repealed. Party-specific tax/incentive programmes follow the governing subparty. Built factories and infrastructure remain national assets.

lifecycles.title: Sugar, diversification and Soviet supply
rules: Default Sugar and Soviet Oil: agriculture +10%, sanction resistance âˆ’10%, foreign influence defence âˆ’10%.

Food before Sugar only: replace it with Imported Machinery, agriculture +0%, sanction resistance âˆ’4%, foreign influence defence âˆ’5%. Light Industry only: agriculture +5%, sanction resistance âˆ’6%, foreign influence defence âˆ’6%. Both completed: agriculture +0%, sanction resistance âˆ’2%, foreign influence defence âˆ’3%. Exactly one variant is active.

A Soviet supply shock requires an actual withdrawal of a recorded support/supply commitment or a verified contraction of bilateral fuel/trade deliveries. Calendar year 1990 and CMEA exit alone are insufficient. The counterpart must control withdrawal; no new autonomous annual subsidy is assumed.

While the verified shortage remains: no diversification gives civilian productivity âˆ’20%, construction âˆ’15%, agriculture âˆ’8%; one of Food before Sugar/Light Industry gives âˆ’12%, âˆ’10%, âˆ’4%; both gives âˆ’6%, âˆ’5%, âˆ’2%. These replace one another and clear when deliveries recover or a substitute supply accord actually takes effect.
The 1990 emergency choice adds only its stated 365-day adjustment. It does not add the modern Special Period idea or repeat the shock under another name.

lifecycles.title: The embargo and diplomatic easing
rules: The custom embargo spirit is the fallback representation of the US restriction. If an active native US embargo or an Imperia comprehensive US economic sanction already supplies that restriction, suspend this fallback and use that system. Third-country sanctions remain separate.
Limited accepted easing: replace the fallback with resource export revenue âˆ’10%, civilian productivity âˆ’3%; reciprocal opinion +10. Claims commission costs CUB 0.10 Treasury.

Full accepted executive trade settlement in 1970â€“90: remove actual US embargo restrictions and this fallback, reciprocal opinion +20. CUB pays a total 0.25 Treasury (only a further 0.15 if the earlier 0.10 commission was paid). Restore the fallback if comprehensive restrictions are subsequently reimposed.
MFN tariff treatment, official credits, private claims and GuantÃ¡namo require their own terms. The later 1996 statutory codification is not a retroactive Congress-only embargo gate.

lifecycles.title: Security institutions
rules: The initial CDR/security institution remains a national starting constraint. A professional settlement through Socialist Constitution, Accountable Officers or Professional Intelligence replaces it with counterintelligence defence +10%, political power gain âˆ’4%, research âˆ’2%.

A completed civilian constitutional settlement (AutÃ©ntico, Ortodoxo, Christian Democrat, Liberal, RECE charter or Alpha civic-demobilisation endpoint) replaces that institution with civilian counterintelligence defence +5% and weekly bureaucracy expenditure +3%. The institutional replacement is persistent, not a second party buff.

An explicit later surveillance-restoration decision must replace the institution again and pay its political cost; merely changing a party does not resurrect dismantled institutions. Party programme modifiers still deactivate/reactivate with the exact current slot.

lifecycles.title: Exile and dialogue
rules: The exile spirit begins at workforce âˆ’4%, stability âˆ’3%. A completed voluntary family/return agreement plus actual registered returns reduces it to workforce âˆ’2%, stability âˆ’1%. A dialogue announcement alone grants only its listed event effects.

Historical migration totals are context, not an automatic population debit. All departures and returns pass once through the existing native/Imperia migration ledger; forced removal is not a selectable development reward.

lifecycles.title: Budget and corruption caps
rules: A valid budget tier is required in availability and completion. Below cap use the native +1 tier helper. At edu_05/health_06 use one named sector-efficiency idea giving âˆ’3% weekly sector expenditure. Repeated cap rewards reuse that same idea and never stack.

Corruption reform calls decrease_corruption only at corruption_level_02 through _10. At _01 use a single named Public Oversight idea: weekly bureaucracy expenditure âˆ’3%. Missing law category blocks enactment and requests initialization; no helper is allowed to fall through to unrelated +150 political power.
These national service/oversight institutions remain after a government leaves. Their recurring budget obligations remain real; completed grants cannot be farmed by switching parties.

lifecycles.title: Fidel-era social, scientific and economic programmes
rules: The Family Code completion records a legal reform. Its funded childcare/work-participation modifier is a governing programme; switching parties does not automatically repeal family rights. Actual repeal requires its own political decision.

Family Doctor Teams grants a native healthcare budget tier once, after the same valid-tier and cap guards as other health reforms. The law tier persists across governments; the PCC coordination/cost modifiers follow the exact governing slot. No healthcare tax-income modifier is described as clinical care.

The Biological Front grants a single 50% CAT_genetics research bonus and one civilian factory in State 854 after legal construction/payment checks. Both are durable national gains; the weekly research-training expenditure is part of the current PCC programme. Refresh never repeats the factory or research use.

Peasant Markets follows continued SDPE; Revive Microbrigades follows Rectification. Their ancestors are mutually exclusive, so both economic programmes cannot stack. The 1986 congress event respects the completed verdict and never grants either new follow-up as a second bonus.

The microbrigade infrastructure level represents Havana neighbourhood utilities/access works. Construction speed, redirected civilian output and welfare expenditure model the mobilisation programme; no apartment count or housing-stock system is invented.

lifecycles.title: Government lifecycle and international agreements
rules: Each governmental programme uses the exact ruling_party slot in availability and reward. Completed receipts persist; current modifiers are rebuilt from the receipts of the current slot only.

Government change refresh, initial load and weekly reconciliation remove inactive party dynamic modifiers and restore eligible ones. Refresh contains no Treasury, debt, construction, research, experience, law-tier or migration grant.

CMEA member programme requires the actual admission spirit, including in the reward and subsequent refresh. Leaving suspends it; readmission restores the programme but never repeats its research grant.

Accepted technical/cultural support runs until terminated by its diplomatic terms. An offer focus only creates a 90-day recipient-owned proposal; refusal or expiry charges nobody. Every accepted transaction has a once-only receipt and validates ownership/control/caps before charging.
Approval concept only: no live focus, idea, event, party registry or country history is changed.
Government branches use exact ruling_party slots 4,6,19,22,3,18,1,2,0,20,5,7,13. Slot4/Fidel is the historical start. No already-ruling-party unlock focus.

Exile governments require an actual existing-party transition through negotiated opening, elite/security rupture, or externally settled conflict. A focus does not create a domestic opposition majority.

Programme receipts persist. Active party modifiers turn off when that subparty leaves office and reactivate on return. Physical assets, research grants and payments execute once only, outside refresh helpers.
Shared national institutions remain unless explicitly repealed. Knowledge and healthcare do not vanish merely because a party loses office.
Native budget tier upgrades use actual below-cap checks. At the cap show and apply a defined service-efficiency alternative, not the helper's unrelated PP fallback.
Construction rechecks actual owned/controlled state, slots or building cap before charging; native cancel_if_invalid remains enabled. A changed target cannot consume money without delivery.
Money costs are one-time MD Treasury units unless explicitly labelled weekly. Percentage expenditure effects modify the existing weekly native budget; no annual literal is copied into a weekly tick.
All counterpart offers are recipient-owned, expire after 90 days, revalidate on acceptance and have explicit refusal. A completed proposal focus is never an accepted treaty receipt.

The early harvest cannot be declared failed on 1 January. 26 July1970 resolves the campaign; 1972 island naming is a genuine dated commemorative action. Other chapter dates are historical notes, not arbitrary tree locks.

Soviet trade contraction triggers exposure-sensitive emergency choices; there is no inevitable 1990 collapse if the player diversified. Dollar legalisation and post-1993 tourism systems are not historical 1970â€“90 rewards.

OSPAAAL, MININT and JUCEPLAN have compact programmes for their registered governing slots; these are alternate institutional governments, not claims that they were independent mass parties. CTC, FMC, CDRs, Church and scientists enter as institutions. Tiny registry-only religious/monarchist/neo-fascist circles receive no national branch.
